sections.title: Root lama and the abbots of Menri
sections.blurb: Figure 1 is the root lama Shenlha Ökar; figures 2–34 are the abbots of Menri Monastery, each listed with the year he became abbot (master numbering 1–34).

entries.name: Shenlha Ökar
entries.desc: The glorious teacher who has blessings and who has the nature of all of the collective Victorious Ones, the all-good essence of the kind root lama, Shenlha Ökar. He has the 25 mudra of the Perfected Enjoyment Body. He wears the 13 peaceful ornaments and has the 9 ways of purity. He has the 32 major marks and the 80 minor marks. He has the 40 items of nobility and he radiates forth a million rays of light.

sections.title: Aural Transmission of Zhang Zhung
sections.blurb: The Zhang Zhung Nyen Gyü: the continuous, unbroken Aural Lineage of Dzogchen teachings. The post numbers it 1–101 (the list below has 102 entries).

entries.name: Küntu Zangpo
entries.desc: The source of the lineage, the teacher Küntu Zangpo. This is the Bönku. He is naked and without ornamentation.
entries.group: Nine Divine Beings of the Mind-to-Mind Transmission

entries.name: Shenlha Ökar
entries.desc: The pure, white light deity of compassion. This is the Dzok ku. His compassion is all-pervasive and he is the embodiment of exalted, positive qualities.
entries.group: Nine Divine Beings of the Mind-to-Mind Transmission

entries.name: Gyalwa Shenrap
entries.desc: The divine being that descended to the human realm in order to guide sentient beings. This is the Tulku and he became known as the Lord Tönpa Shenrap Miwoché.
entries.group: Nine Divine Beings of the Mind-to-Mind Transmission

entries.name: Tsemé Öden
entries.desc: The divine being that emanated into a god realm in order to guide bodhisattvas.
entries.group: Nine Divine Beings of the Mind-to-Mind Transmission

entries.name: Trulshen Nangden
entries.desc: The divine being that emanated into a god realm from the mind of Küntu Zangpo.
entries.group: Nine Divine Beings of the Mind-to-Mind Transmission

entries.name: Barnang Khujuk
entries.desc: The divine being that emanated into a god realm from the speech of Küntu Zangpo
entries.group: Nine Divine Beings of the Mind-to-Mind Transmission

entries.name: Zangza Ringtsun
entries.desc: A divine emanation of the Great Mother Sherap Chamma and the divine mother of Chimé Tsukpü. Trulshen nangden descended upon her right shoulder in the form of a turquoise cuckoo and caused a subtle, internal heat. One year later, she gave birth to Chimé Tsukpü. Her body color is golden and she holds a golden vase in her right hand and a golden mala in her left hand.
entries.group: Nine Divine Beings of the Mind-to-Mind Transmission

entries.name: Chimé Tsukpü
entries.desc: He is turquoise in color. Nine days after his birth, his mother Zangza Ringtsun found him suspended in space and radiating light. He taught both tantra and Dzogchen.
entries.group: Nine Divine Beings of the Mind-to-Mind Transmission

entries.name: Sangwa Düpa
entries.desc: He received the transmission through rikpa and was the first to use speech as well as awareness to transmit the teachings. He was born a prince of Tazik and began the transmission among human beings. Because he was the first to use speech to transmit the teachings, he is also known as The Teacher of the Aural Transmission Lineage.
entries.group: Nine Divine Beings of the Mind-to-Mind Transmission

entries.name: Lhabön Yongsu Dakpa
entries.desc: He received the transmission from Sangwa Düpa and spread the teachings in the god realm.

entries.name: Lübön Banam
entries.desc: He received the transmission from Sangwa Düpa and spread the teachings in the lü (Sanskrit. naga) realm.

entries.name: Mibön Tridé Zambu
entries.desc: He received the transmission from Sangwa Düpa and spread the teachings in the human realm.

entries.name: Trisho Gyalwa
entries.desc: He was the son of Banam Kyolpo.

entries.name: Tapihritsa
entries.desc: He was born into a nomadic family in the country of Zhang Zhung. He practiced at a place near Mt. Tise known as Sengé Tap. He practiced for nine years without interrupting it with ordinary, human speech. He achieved the rainbow body of light. After this, Tapihritsa manifested as a young boy and began working as a shepherd for a wealthy man in the area where Nangzher Lopo was practicing. Upon meeting, Nangzher Lopo asked the boy a series of questions and became annoyed at his answers. Challenging him to debate in front of the Zhang Zhung king, the boy laughed and began speaking about the true nature of mind. Realizing that this was an emanation and not an ordinary boy, Nangzher Lopo fainted. Regaining consciousness, he saw that the boy had transformed and was showing a clear and luminous body surrounded by a rainbow and suspended in space.
entries.imgcap: Lineage Masters of the Aural Transmission of Zhang Zhung prior to the 8th Century

entries.name: Gyerpung Nangzher Lopo
entries.desc: He extensively practiced the cycles of Zhang Zhung Meri and Gekho. In doing so, he acquired great magical power. He was the priest for the Zhang Zhung king and was well-known throughout the kingdom. Because of his devotion, he met and received teachings from Tapihritsa 3 times. He lived for 573 years.
entries.imgcap: Lineage Masters of the Aural Transmission of Zhang Zhung prior to the 8th Century

entries.name: Gyalzik Sechung
entries.desc: He first received these teachings when he was 72 years old. He lived for 317 years and attained the rainbow body of light.
entries.group: The Six Yogis of Zhang Zhung (before the 8th century)
entries.imgcap: Lineage Masters of the Aural Transmission of Zhang Zhung prior to the 8th Century

entries.name: Mu Shen Tsogé
entries.desc: At the age of 3, Nangzher Lopo identified him as a qualified student and he received the teachings at the age of 19. He lived for 173 years and attained the rainbow body of light.
entries.group: The Six Yogis of Zhang Zhung (before the 8th century)
entries.imgcap: Lineage Masters of the Aural Transmission of Zhang Zhung prior to the 8th Century

entries.name: Mu Gyershen Tsotang
entries.desc: He lived for 113 years and attained the rainbow body of light.
entries.group: The Six Yogis of Zhang Zhung (before the 8th century)
entries.imgcap: Lineage Masters of the Aural Transmission of Zhang Zhung prior to the 8th Century

entries.name: Mu Shotram Chenpo
entries.desc: He lived for 117 years and attained the rainbow body.
entries.group: The Six Yogis of Zhang Zhung (before the 8th century)
entries.imgcap: Lineage Masters of the Aural Transmission of Zhang Zhung prior to the 8th Century

entries.name: Mu Gyalwa Lodro
entries.desc: He was attendant to Mu Shotram Chenpo for nine years before he received teachings. He lived for 270 years and attained the rainbow body of light.
entries.group: The Six Yogis of Zhang Zhung (before the 8th century)
entries.imgcap: Lineage Masters of the Aural Transmission of Zhang Zhung prior to the 8th Century

entries.name: Pongyal Tsenpo
entries.desc: Also known as Ponchen Tsenpo, He purified all the defilements of his physical body and therefore it was not necessary for him to eat food for nourishment. He lived for 1,600 years and his body showed no signs of aging. He then transformed himself into a turquoise cuckoo and flew off towards the southwest in order to subdue demons.
entries.group: The Six Yogis of Zhang Zhung (before the 8th century)
entries.imgcap: Lineage Masters of the Aural Transmission of Zhang Zhung prior to the 8th Century

entries.name: Gugé Loden
entries.desc: He received the teachings from Pöngyal Tsenpo in an area near Mount Tisé. As a youth, he worked as a goatherd and had often dreamt of a blue cuckoo speaking to him. One day, he watched as a cuckoo descended from the sky near him. Going closer, instead of a bird, he found a yogi in a blue robe. This was Pöngyal Tsenpo.
entries.group: Upper system: the Six Realized Sages

entries.name: Pureng Kunga
entries.desc: He practiced in the area of Mount Tisé. By following his lama’s guidance on Dzogchen, he attained realization in one month.
entries.group: Upper system: the Six Realized Sages

entries.name: Naljor Sechok
entries.desc: He had the power to prolong his life span and displayed many miracles.
entries.group: Upper system: the Six Realized Sages

entries.name: Kyungji Mutur
entries.desc: He was a wandering yogi without any particular place of practice.
entries.group: Upper system: the Six Realized Sages

entries.name: Dewa Ringmo
entries.group: Upper system: the Six Realized Sages

entries.name: Tokmé Zhikpo
entries.desc: He lived most of his life in a cave. He gave the full transmission to Yangtön Sherap Gyaltsen. This same lama also received the full transmission of the Lower system of transmission. In this way, he reunited the two transmissions.
entries.group: Upper system: the Six Realized Sages

entries.name: Shengyal Lhatse
entries.desc: He lived for 113 years.

entries.name: Lhagom Karpo
entries.desc: He lived for 97 years.

entries.name: Ngodrup Gyaltsen
entries.desc: He was the son of Lhagom Karpo. He asked his father for teachings but his father refused and told him that he had performed a divination that indicated that his son was not a good candidate. Ngodrup then abandoned his wife and child and went to study with a Buddhist. Soon after this, his father reconsidered his decision and agreed to teach him. He lived for 73 years.

entries.name: Orgom Kündul
entries.desc: Few Bönpo followers sought teachings from him but many Buddhist practitioners sought him out. He lived for 80 years.

entries.name: Yangtön Sherap Gyaltsen
entries.desc: He was born into the prestigious Yangtön lineage of Dolpo, Nepal. He lived and taught during the 11th century. He received the full transmissions of both the Upper and the Lower Systems of Transmission and therefore united the transmissions. Out of compassion, he wrote down some of the teachings as well as commentaries. According to prophecy, his life span was to be 75 years but due to writing down the secret teachings, he died at the age of 63.
entries.group: Yangtön Sherap Gyaltsen: the two systems reunite

entries.name: Dampa Bumjé
entries.desc: He spread the Bön teachings in the areas of Dolpo, Mustang and Western Tibet. His father was Yangtön Sherap Gyaltsen. After his death, Dampa received teachings from his mother. Because of his extraordinary meditative experiences, he added his own teachings to those of his father in the Experiential Transmission.
entries.group: The Five Masters of the Mantra and the Mind (southern lineage)

entries.name: Lu Drakpa Tashi Gyaltsen
entries.desc: He was also a son to Yangtön Sherap Gyaltsen. Unlike his brother, he was a wandering yogi. He lived for 85 years.
entries.group: The Five Masters of the Mantra and the Mind (southern lineage)

entries.name: Tokden Wonpo Yeshe Gyaltsen
entries.desc: His mother was Yangtön Sherap Gyaltsen’s daughter. His father was a bandit and he joined him in his exploits. One day, he father was killed during a fight and he was badly wounded. Once he recovered, he began to seek revenge. After some time had passed, he became tired with fighting and went to his uncle, Dampa Bumjé, to learn to read so that he could read the scriptures. However, his progress was slow and he went to his other uncle, Lu Drakpa, and asked for teachings that didn’t require the ability to read. Having received the teachings of the Zhang Zhung Nyen Gyü, he practiced and attained realization.
entries.group: The Five Masters of the Mantra and the Mind (southern lineage)

entries.name: Yangtön Gyaltsen Rinchen
entries.desc: From the age of 8 until 21, he practiced tantra. At the age of 21, he received the Dzogchen teachings. He founded the monastery of Samling in Dolpo, Nepal.
entries.group: The Five Masters of the Mantra and the Mind (southern lineage)

entries.name: Chikchö Depa Sherap
entries.desc: He is also known as Tokden Depa Sherap. He practiced in the area of Mount Tisé among other places.
entries.group: The Five Masters of the Mantra and the Mind (southern lineage)

entries.name: Druchen Gyalwa Yungdrung
entries.desc: 1242–1290. He was one of four brothers and received monk’s vows from his older brother. He was once the abbot of Yeru Wensaka Monastery which was founded by his family. He organized the practices of the Zhang Zhung Nyen Gyü into a widely used practice manual commonly known as the Chak Tri. He wrote many prayers, ritual guides and commentaries.

entries.name: Ripa Sherap Lodro
entries.desc: He was from Dolpo and traveled a great deal throughout Tibet.

entries.name: Rangdrol Lama Gyaltsen
entries.desc: He frequently debated Buddhist monks including Tsongkhapa.

entries.name: A Tok Sherap Gyaltsen
entries.desc: He was the personal attendant to Dru Gyalwa Yungdrung. He showed many signs of realization and lived for 120 years.

entries.name: Patön Tengyal Zangpo
entries.desc: He showed many signs of realization and is said to have circumambulated Mount Tisé in the form of a vulture.

sections.title: Three-fold Cycle of Dzogchen Proclamations
sections.blurb: The Dzogchen Drakpa Korsum Gyü, numbered 1–28; it ends with Nyammé Sherap Gyaltsen (28) at the base of the columns.

entries.name: Shenlha Ökar
entries.desc: The source of the lineage, the White Light Deity, Shenlha Ökar. He appears in the form of dzok ku, the enlightened Body of the Perfected Qualities and wears the corresponding ornaments. His compassion is all-pervasive.

entries.name: The Five Victorious Families
entries.desc: Also known as the Five Buddha Families; they have gone beyond bliss.

entries.name: Chimé Tsukphü
entries.desc: He was the previous existence of the enlightened Lord Tönpa Shenrab Miwoche immediately before descending from heaven to earth.

entries.name: Lhashen Yongsu Dakpa
entries.desc: He was the shen of the gods who received the teachings from Chimé Tsukphü.

entries.name: Milu Samlek
entries.desc: He was the shen of the humans who received the teachings from Chime Tsukphü. He was born a prince in the ancient land of Tazik as his father, the king, was about to die. He was known for his intelligence even as a young man.

entries.name: Lushen Yeshé Nyingpo
entries.desc: He is the shen of the lu, aka nagas, who received the teachings from Chime Tsukphü.

entries.name: Ödzer Pakmé
entries.desc: He was a master from Tazik.

entries.name: Sangwa Düpa
entries.desc: He was a chief disciple of Chimé Tsukphü. He was born a prince of Tazik.

entries.name: Tonggyung Tüchen
entries.imgcap: Translator and great yogi, Lama Tonggyung Tuchen

entries.name: Nyachen Lishu Taring
entries.desc: A king and queen found a beautiful young girl in a forest. They named her Takza Liwer. Some time later, through the performance of ritual, she transformed herself into a man. However, she was still female when she wrote the root text for The Three-fold Cycle of Dzogchen Proclamations in the 8th century. As a male, he became heir to the kingdom and was called Nyachen Lishu Taring.

entries.name: Zhotön Ngödrup Drakpa
entries.desc: He was an emanation of Lishu Taring and a tertön, or treasure revealer, who rediscovered hidden texts behind a statue of Vairochana in Lhodrak that were hidden by Lishu Taring during a time of persecution for the Yungdrung Bön.

entries.name: Nyammé Sherap Gyaltsen
entries.desc: The Second Victor and founder of Tashi Menri Monastery, 1356–1415.

sections.title: Profound Guidance through AH
sections.blurb: The AH Tri, one of three Dzogchen lineages of the Yungdrung Bön tradition. Figures 1–14 and 16–21 run down the column; 15 is Nyammé Sherap Gyaltsen at its base.

entries.name: Me’u Gongdzö Ritropa
entries.desc: Founder of the lineage, Me’u Gongdzö Ritropa. He is often referred to simply as Dampa, “The Sage” or “The Saint”. He exhibited many signs of accomplishment such as flying through the sky and leaving his hand and foot prints in stone. Although his primary focus was upon his meditation, he also wrote a number of texts. In addition to material he collected from other sources, he added his own gong ter, or mind treasure, to this collection. He organized the practice of the A Tri into 80 meditation sessions.
entries.imgcap: Founder of the AH Tri Lineage of Dzogchen teachings, The Saint, The Supreme Gongdzo Ritropa Rinpoche

entries.name: Gomchen Barwa
entries.desc: He was an unconventional person and became a great yogi. He was known for odd and somewhat dramatic displays. One day, Gongdzo Ritropa took Gomchen to a grassy area that was quite wet. The lama knew that Gomchen was known to have been quite athletic in his youth. So he told him to make a great leap. In doing so, Gomchen slipped and violently fell down. In that very instant, he achieved spiritual realization without interruption. Rather than taking ordination, he remained a laymen his entire life. He had many disciples and attained the rainbow body of light.

entries.name: Drogön Yorpo Mepal
entries.desc: He composed a commentary for the Guidance through AH teachings.

entries.name: A Zha Lodro Gyaltsen
entries.desc: 1198–1263. He condensed the number of meditation sessions to 30.

entries.name: Druchen Gyalwa Yungdrung
entries.desc: 1242–1290. A.D. He was born into the Dru family in the area of Yeru Wensaka in Central Tibet. He received his monk vows from his older brother, Dru Dulwa Rinpoche. He was once the abbot of Yeru Wensaka Monastery which was founded by his family. He further condensed the number of meditation sessions of the Guidance through AH to 15 and composed the fundamental practice text “AH Tri Practice in 15 Sessions”.

entries.name: Dru Namkha Odzer
entries.desc: He was the younger brother of Dru Gyalwa Yungdrung.

entries.name: Dru Sonam Gyaltsen
entries.desc: 1268–1321. He was the nephew of Dru Gyalwa Yungdrung.

entries.name: Rinchen Lodro
entries.desc: His mother was from the Dru family.

entries.name: Nyammé Sherap Gyaltsen
entries.desc: 1356–1415. He is known as the Second Buddha and founded Tashi Menri Monastery in Tibet.

entries.name: Rinchen Gyaltsen
entries.desc: He became abbot of Menri Monastery in 1415.

entries.name: Namkha Yeshe
entries.desc: He became abbot of Menri Monastery in 1446.

entries.name: Kunzang Gyaltsen
entries.desc: He became abbot of Menri Monastery in 1464.

sections.title: Lamas of Pure Discipline (Monastic Lineage)
sections.blurb: The lineage of monastic discipline: masters who took monk’s vows. 1–50 run down the column; 51 is Nyammé Sherap Gyaltsen.

entries.name: Tritsuk Gyalwa
entries.desc: 16,017 BC – 7,817 BC. This is the name that the enlightened Lord Tönpa Shenrap Miwoche received upon taking ordination as a monk at the age of 31. Although he was already a completely enlightened being, he showed the example of taking the path of renunciation.
entries.group: From Tritsuk Gyalwa to Me’u Gongdzö Ritropa
entries.imgcap: Lord Tonpa Shenrap showing the path of renunciation as the monk Tritsuk Gyalwa

entries.name: Tsukshen Gyalwa
entries.group: From Tritsuk Gyalwa to Me’u Gongdzö Ritropa

entries.name: Drangsong Gyalwa
entries.desc: He was one of Tönpa Shenrap’s eight sons. His birth name was Tobu Bumsang.
entries.group: From Tritsuk Gyalwa to Me’u Gongdzö Ritropa

entries.name: Tsukse Mawo

entries.name: Muzi Salzang
entries.desc: He was a manifestation of Mucho Demdruk. During a time of suppression, he retreated to a cave and went into a meditation of cessation, stopping all thoughts and sensations. Hundreds of years later, Tribar Tsultrim came upon him in the cave.

entries.name: Tribar Tsultrim
entries.desc: He was the manifestation of Tsukshen Gyalwa. He was born a prince but due to external circumstances, he was banished to Mongolia and became a slave of a local ruler. One day, while looking after the ruler’s horses, he wandered into a cave that looked dark at the entrance but light on the inside. Once inside the cave, he saw a figure that resembled a monk but whose hair had grown down to the ground and become entangled. The karmic connection immediately ripened and he joyfully began prostrating and requesting that the monk awake from his meditation. Day after day, he returned to the cave. First, one of the monk’s eyebrows moved, then a portion of his face. On the third day, he yelled at the slave, “Are you a human or non-human obstacle?” The slave replied that he desired to become his disciple. The monk agreed and gave him full ordination. The monk in the cave was Muzi Selzang.

entries.name: Lachen Mutur
entries.desc: He was born in 952 AD. He was also known by his monastic name, Sherap Tsultrim. He had many disciples, both Yungdrung Bön and Buddhist. He gave his disciples the four signs of monastic ordination which were, Upper and lower garments, a lotus hat and a meditation mat that were all blue. He said that if the articles could not be entirely blue, then they should have parallel seams of blue thread. He was a manifestation of Mutsa Trahé.

sections.blurb: The lineage of tantra: masters who wore the clothes of yogis, tertöns (revealers of hidden treasure) or monks.

entries.name: Trulshen Nangden
entries.desc: Trulshen Nangden was the incarnation of Lord Tönpa Shenrap before he manifested in Olmo Lungrik. Transforming himself into a blue cuckoo, he alighted upon the shoulder of the deity Zangza Ringtsun. This caused a subtle, internal heat. As a result, he was miraculously born to her as Chimé Tsukpü.

entries.name: Zangza Ringtsun
entries.desc: Zangza Ringtsun was an emanation of the enlightened wise, loving Mother, Sherap Chamma who received the teachings of the Secret Mother Tantra from the primordial Buddha.

entries.name: Chimé Tsukpü
entries.desc: Chimé Tsukpü was miraculously born to Zangza Ringtsun.

entries.name: Sangwa Düpa
entries.desc: Sangwa Düpa is cited in some texts as the previous incarnation of Buddha Shakyamuni.

entries.name: Takla Mebar
entries.desc: Takla Mebar was a prince of Tazik.

entries.name: Lhashen Yongsu Dakpa
entries.desc: Lhashen Yongsu Dakpa spread the teachings among the gods.

entries.name: Milu Samlek
entries.desc: Milu Samlek was known for his intelligence and wrote separate commentaries for each of the three cycles of the Mother Tantra: outer, inner, and secret. He spread the teachings in the human realm.

entries.name: Ludrup Yeshe Nyingpo
entries.desc: Ludrup Yeshe Nyingpo was born to parents who had been childless for a long time. After making offerings and praying to the lu, or naga, a child was born to them. He spead the teachings among the lu.
entries.imgcap: Lama Ludrup Yeshe Nyingpo

entries.name: Nangwa Dokchen
entries.desc: Nangwa Dokchen transmitted the teachings to the son of the first Tibetan king.

entries.name: Mutri Tsenpo
entries.desc: Mutri Tsenpo was the son of the first Tibetan king, Nyatri Tsenpo. He invited one hundred eight esteemed scholars of Zhang Zhung to Tibet. After him, these teachings were not taught for three generations due to political obstacles.

entries.name: Hara Chipar
entries.desc: Hara Chipar received the teachings from the four magical khandro of the elements of earth, fire, water and air in order to keep the teachings from further decline.

entries.name: Takwer Liwer
entries.desc: Takwer Liwer was a female practitioner and achieved supernatural powers. She could tame wild animals and also transform herself into anything that she wished. The spirits of earth and water obeyed her commands. After living for three hundred sixty years, she achieved the fruit of realization, the rainbow body of light.

entries.name: Anu Traktak
entries.desc: Anu Traktak practiced on Mount Tise (Kailash) and lived for two hundred fifty-five years.

entries.name: Sené Ga’u
entries.desc: Sené Ga’u was born in Zhang Zhung and had many teachers. It is said that he could cure leprosy simply by looking at the patient. He achieved the rainbow body of light.

entries.name: Tami Teké
entries.desc: Tami Teké lived for two hundred seventy-seven years and achieved supernatural powers.

entries.name: Shebu Rakhuk
entries.desc: Shebu Rakhuk lived for two hundred years and achieved supernatural powers.

entries.name: Zingwa Tüchen
entries.desc: Zingwa Tüchen was a Chinese practitioner and lived for two hundred sixty-one years.

entries.name: Pébön Toktrul
entries.desc: Pébön Toktrul lived for one hundred thirty-five years.

entries.name: Shari Uchen
entries.desc: Shari Uchen was a previous manifestation of the modern day saint, Shardza Tashi Gyaltsen Rinpoche.

entries.name: Mutsa Gyermé
entries.desc: Mutsa Gyermé gave the text Zi Ji to the 14th century master, Loden Nyingpo in a vision.

entries.name: Drenpa Namkha
entries.desc: Drenpa Namkha was born in 753 AD. In general, there are three Drenpa Namkha that are incarnations of the previous one. 1) Drenpa Namkha of Tazik 2)Drenpa Namkha of Zhang Zhung who was a prince and is commonly referred to as La Chen, the great lama. It was this Drenpa Namkha that married an Indian Brahman girl and had twin sons, Tsewang Rikdzin and Pema Tongdrol. 3) Drenpa Namkha of Tibet who saved many Yungdrung Bön texts from destruction during the persecution of Bön by the Tibetan kind Trisong Detsen. See previous post, “Practice of the Great Lama, Drenpa Namkha.”
entries.imgcap: Lama Drenpa Namkha

entries.name: Shenchen Luga
entries.desc: Shenchen Luga (996–1035) was a manifestation of Tonggyung Tüchen and was a terton, or treasure discoverer, one who discovers texts and/or sacred objects that are hidden. He had many disciples who began religious centers in their respective home villages.

entries.name: Germi Nyi Öd
entries.desc: Germi Nyi Öd was born in Zhang Zhung and was a terton. He lived for three hundred years.

entries.name: Matön Sidzin
entries.desc: Matön Sidzin was a terton who discovered many texts including a ritual invocation of the protector Sipe Gyalmo.

entries.name: Yiltön Khyungö Tsal
entries.desc: Yiltön Khyungö Tsal was born in 1198 and was a great terton who discovered many texts including the main ritual text for the protector and yidam Gekho,

entries.name: Wangden Zhuye Lekpo
entries.desc: Wangden Zhuye Lekpo was one of Shenchen Luga’s main disciples and served him as an attendant. He founded the famous Ri Zhing Monastery.

entries.name: Patön Palchok Zangpo
entries.desc: Patön Palchok Zangpo was one of the final disciples to meet Shenchen Luga.

entries.name: Me’u Lhari Nyenpo
entries.desc: Me’u Lhari Nyenpo composed a summary of the long version of the Yungdrung Bön Prajnaparamita that was discovered as terma by Shenchen Luga.

entries.name: Drusha Khyungi Gyaltsen
entries.desc: Drusha Khyungi Gyaltsen was the son of Druchen Namkha Yungdrung.

entries.name: Drogön Lodro Gyaltsen
entries.desc: Drogön Lodro Gyaltsen (1198–1263) was also known as Azha Lodro Gyaltsen.

entries.name: Gyalwa Shenrap Miwo Künlé Nampar Gyalwa
entries.desc: The Completely Victorious in Every Way, Shenrap Miwo. 16,017 BC – 7,817 BC. He is the Enlightened Being of the present time and founder of the Yungdrung Bön religious tradition. He appeared in the human realm when the human life-span was generally 100 years long. There are three versions of his life history: short, medium and long. The short version is within a text commonly referred to as the Do Dü. It is a terma, or rediscovered text, and has twenty-four chapters within one volume. The medium length version is within a text commonly referred to as the Zer Mik. It is also a terma and has eighteen chapters in two volumes. The long version is within a text commonly referred to as the Zi Ji. It is part of a group of orally transmitted texts and has sixty-one chapters in twelve volumes.

entries.name: Dakpa Togyal Yékhyen

entries.name: Jamden Rangma Médron
entries.desc: This Enlightened Being is prophesized to be the Buddha of the Future and will appear in this world when the human life-span has declined to be only 10 years long. He was the younger brother of Tönpa Shenrap Miwo in the celestial realm. He is depicted upon a throne held aloft by elephants and seated upon cushions of a sun, moon, and lotus. His right hand is held in a mudra of contemplation at the center of his heart and his left hand is held in the mudra of equipoise. His body is the color of clear crystal and upon his head is a crown of precious jewels.

entries.name: Dung Tsop Mucho Démdruk
entries.desc: He is the Speech manifestation of the Enlightened Lord Tönpa Shenrap. In the Wood Dragon year of 6016 B.C., he descended from Ölmo Lungrik to the earth in order to benefit sentient beings. This was 1,801 years after Lord Tönpa Shenrap showed the appearance of passing into parinirvana. During this time, many scholars appeared. In the Water Rabbit year of 5717 B.C., he went to the realm of the demi-gods in order to give teachings.
